head: Two runs died
on rate limits
in a week.
body: Not because the work was too big.
Because the most expensive model in the fleet was doing the rowing.

head: A captain who
*never rows
slides.caption: Its value is entirely in where it points. Mutiny, meaning letting the captain pick up an oar, sinks the ship and the token budget in the same afternoon.

head: Not a ladder.
A set of
*roles.
body: Capability is what you need for one hard decision. Volume is what you need for four hundred easy ones.
Those are different problems, and reading tiers as a quality ladder answers only the first one.

items.title: Cheapest tier that covers it
items.sub: not the best available. the cheapest sufficient.

items.title: Escalate exactly one rung
items.sub: on verified failure or real spec ambiguity

items.title: Never escalate on volume
items.sub: volume means go down a tier and parallelise

items.title: Keep the top tier for deciding
items.sub: its value is entirely in where it points

head: One sentence,
made mandatory
code: Delegate execution. Do not perform it.
callout: That reads as permission, and permission loses to the more concrete instruction next to it. A model told to plan and execute will execute.

head: The captain
never rows
body: It has to be said out loud, because a captain built to be helpful will pick up an oar.
It will look like enthusiasm right up until the ship stops steering.
